title: Normalized proper/open coefficient pasting
statement: For a flat morphism a:Λ→Λ′ of commutative condensed rings, a compactification refinement r:c→d, and a bounded constructible Λ_X-object K, assume its scalar extension is bounded constructible. The explicit proper/open paste consisting of the proper scalar mate for d.g, its direct image of the three-map coefficient/open-lift comparison, and the original transported target compositor equals the projection for d followed by the original Λ′ refinement at the scalar extension of K. This is the open-lift half of the argument; it assumes no coefficient compatibility of the source proper-image compositor. All constructions are the original maps of [def-pur-condensed-compact-support-projection-core].

source.place: Agent-formulated constituent of the coefficient/refinement compatibility argument in def-pur-condensed-compact-support-projection, original Steps 15–16. Not claimed as a literal theorem of Bhatt–Scholze.

proof.text: compare the normalized lift after scalar extension with the normalized lift for the scalar-extended bounded constructible object. Precompose the former with the inverse open scalar comparison for `d.i` and transpose under the open adjunction with coefficients `Λ'`. The open scalar mate equation carries the original open unit to the new open unit. The proper scalar mate equation carries the original proper counit to the new proper counit. Restriction of coefficients commutes with the pullback composition comparison associated to `r.i_hom`. Consequently the transpose, followed by `fieldProperOpenRestriction Λ' r`, is the new open unit. Uniqueness of the normalized lift at `⟨(condensedScalar a X).obj K.obj, hK⟩` identifies it with the chosen new lift. Cancel the inverse open comparison. This proves that the three morphisms inside the proper direct image in the displayed left side equal the open comparison for `d.i` followed by the new normalized lift. Apply the proper direct image to that equality, precompose with the proper scalar mate for `d.g`, and postcompose with the specified target pushforward compositor. Functoriality separates the two factors inside that image. The first resulting factor is the component of `condensedProjection a d`; the second is the component of `fieldRefinement Λ' r` at the scalar-extended object, by their definitions. Associativity gives the claimed equality. No invertibility of a proper scalar comparison is assumed.

lean.statement:
theorem fieldProperOpen_scalar_pasting {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    {c d : Compactification f} (r : c.Refinement d)
    (K : BoundedConstructible (condensedRingObj Λ X))
    (hK : boundedConstructible (condensedRingObj Λ' X) ((condensedScalar a X).obj K.obj)) :
    (condensedPushScalar a d.g).app
          ((CondensedRing.openImmersionLowerShriek Λ d.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj K.obj) ≫
        (CondensedRing.lowerStar Λ' d.g).rightDerivedFunctor.map
          ((condensedScalar a d.Z).map (fieldProperOpen Λ r K) ≫
            (condensedPushScalar a r.hom).app
              ((CondensedRing.openImmersionLowerShriek Λ c.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj K.obj) ≫
            (CondensedRing.lowerStar Λ' r.hom).rightDerivedFunctor.map
              ((condensedOpenScalar a c.i).hom.app K.obj)) ≫
        ((fieldPushComp Λ' r.hom d.g).hom ≫
          eqToHom (congrArg (fieldDerivedLowerStar Λ') r.hom_g)).app
            ((CondensedRing.openImmersionLowerShriek Λ' c.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj
              ((condensedScalar a X).obj K.obj)) =
      (condensedProjection a d).app K.obj ≫
        (fieldRefinement Λ' r).app ⟨(condensedScalar a X).obj K.obj, hK⟩
